audit.why: Even (50.9% WR, 4631 games): Sylas bullies all of lane, Vladimir outscales at two-plus items. Text matches.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart holds blanket 'Skill' on rows 0,1,3,5 while content win[] and packet both say Sylas.
audit.why: Content and packet agree; aligned full sides/ratings/whys atomically. win[] already correct so side edited alone per the chart rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool is repeatedly labeled 'E' in the content layer (spikes[1].text, mid, wants.you[1]); it is Vladimir's W. E is Tides of Blood. Also dontsFull[1].t warns of a 'loaded CC' — Vladimir has no hard CC.
audit.why: Kit file: W = Sanguine Pool (28/25/22/19/16s, untargetable 2s), E = Tides of Blood. Grievous Wounds timing matters vs Q/R heal (missing-interactions).
audit.corrected: Slot labels fixed; don't retitled to the pool; anti-heal already present in report[8].

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. It governs your forward steps. - E Abscond (shield-dash) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool (W): 28s at rank 1, 16s max — the untargetable dodge. Bait it and you own a very long kill window. - Tides of Blood (E) costs his own health early — trade right after he charges it. - Hold your R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: E-shield in, E2-chain, Q-W with whirls between, heal out — the full brawl string he answered with one rotation and regret.
edits.after: Hemoplague is a 120-second amp — steal it early and stack both plagues in one all-in his own team never signed up for.

edits.before: Chaining into a loaded CC with W down — Sylas without the heal is a mage who chose melee for the aesthetic.
edits.after: A hoarded Hijack is wasted tempo — a stolen Hemoplague spent on any real fight beats the perfect one that never comes.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling your all-in, healing the trade back with Transfusion, and outscaling into a raid boss.

edits.before: Q-poke the wave contacts — the chain detonation chips while you wait for the real kit at 3.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours — Vladimir pays health for Tides of Blood and has no sustain yet, so poke freely.

edits.before: W joins: the heal-strike makes even trades dishonest — yours refunds, his doesn't.
edits.after: W joins and he still can't punish your Chain Lash — the heal-strike makes trades free.

edits.before: Chain-trade on cooldown: shield in, stun, whirl the passive autos, heal out. The brawl is the plan.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 he is at his weakest — chain-trade on cooldown: shield in, whirl, heal out. Keep bullying.

edits.before: First item spike: full chains with a stolen ult delete or out-brawl anything mid offers.
edits.after: First item spike is yours — Vlad's power arrives a component or two later. Keep forcing.

edits.before: Your level-6 all-in kills him if you bait his E Sanguine Pool first: throw a jab, wait for the pool, then E Abscond in and commit Q-W Kingslayer. R Hijack can steal Hemoplague for extra amp, but your raw combo already blows up his early frame.
edits.after: Your level-6 all-in kills him if you bait his W Sanguine Pool first: throw a jab, wait for the pool, then E Abscond in and commit Q-W Kingslayer. R Hijack can steal Hemoplague for extra amp, but your raw combo already blows up his early frame.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 6 are your kill window: keep short-trading before his sustain scales, and time your all-in around his E Sanguine Pool, which is his only escape. Bait the pool with a jab, then E Abscond in and land Q-W Kingslayer for the execute; Hijacking his Hemoplague adds amp if you want it. Roam when he shoves, since he has no way to follow you cross-map.
